To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new, environmentally benign process for the fractionation of wood pulp has been developed that allows the recovery of cellulose of highest purity and of hemicellulosic polymers without any loss in yield or degradation.

we have developed an efficient method for the separation of cellulose and hemicellulosis from wood pulp by using a combination of a cosolvents and the ionic liquid ionic liquid  1-ethyl-  3- methyl- imidazolium acetat (EMIM O Ac).
the fractionation of wood pulps into cellulose and hemicellulosis is possible by using ionic liquids and cosolvents, without any loss of cellulose.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new, environmentally benign fractionation concepts for wood pulps.
the development of a process for the fractionation of wood pulp into cellulose and hemicellulosic fractions by means of a cosolvents/ionic liquid mixture.

the development of new, efficient and sustainable technologies for the separation of cellulose and hemicellulosis from wood pulp, using the ionic liquid ionic liquid EMIM OAc and water, acetone, and ethanol as cosolvents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ionic liquid EMIM OAc in combination with water and/or ethanol is able to fractionate hemicellulosis from wood pulp in a simple and environmentally friendly manner.

the use of ionic liquids as a fractionation agent for the separation of cellulose and hemicellulosic fractions from paper-grade pulp is an ecologically and technically viable alternative to existing methods.
the presented process is a novel, environmentally friendly, and economically feasible method for the production of high purity cellulose from wood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a process for the production of cellulose of highest purity, starting from paper-grade pulp, which has a hemicellulosis content of 25%.
we have found a way to produce a high purity cellulose from paper grade pulp without any yield losses, depolymerization or chemical treatment.
a new process for the separation of cellulose from wood is introduced.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a cosolvent addition can significantly improve the fractionation process.
the ionic liquid/cellulose system is very stable and can be used for fractionation of cellulose and hemicellulosic pulp.
a cosolvent can be added to an ionic liquid to improve the fractionation process, while the ionic liquid itself can be recycled.
